approach.method_basis: CMA-ES samples candidate points from a multivariate Gaussian, ranks the ones that come back, and moves the distribution itself rather than any individual point. The mean shifts toward a weighted average of the better samples, the covariance matrix adapts so the Gaussian stretches along directions that have been paying off, and a separate cumulative path controls the overall step size. Applied to molecules, the sampled points are latent vectors and each one is turned into a molecule by a frozen autoencoder decoder before scoring.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a 24-dimensional latent with full covariance adaptation rather than a diagonal approximation, so the Gaussian can learn correlated directions in the latent space. It attaches every observed score to the exact latent sample that generated the molecule, uses descending score rank with logarithmic recombination weights, and carries cumulative evolution paths for both covariance and step size across all fourteen generations of an objective.

observed_bottleneck: This lineage has no Parent or evaluated CMA-ES root. Its difficulty is to learn useful correlated search directions from scarce molecular feedback in a latent space whose decoded objective may be discontinuous or highly redundant. The supplied node n-77c41c9bc036 was refuted when online flow adaptation broke its registered exact-token reconstruction invariant, although the failed checks retained canonical molecular identity. That evidence motivates freezing this root's representation and auditing score-to-decoded-sample attachment; it does not establish that a VAE has useful local geometry or that CMA-ES will improve scores.
hypothesis: Sample de novo molecules through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE decoder from an adaptive multivariate Gaussian, attach observed scores to the exact generating latent samples, and update the Gaussian mean, full covariance, and global step size using descending score ranks, weighted recombination, and cumulative evolution paths.

finding_summary.headline: Full covariance adaptation ran exactly and finished eleventh at 0.303, undone by one objective
finding_summary.insights: The optimizer is correct and its budget is the problem. Fourteen generations of twenty scored offspring is a very short run for an algorithm that spends its early generations learning a covariance, so the distribution barely finishes adapting before the budget ends. Its collapse on drd2_docking is informative in a different way: that objective rewards a compact basic amine, and this node's proposals there average eighty characters, nearly double every other objective on the same node. The Gaussian drifted into a region of latent space that decodes to large lipophilic molecules and covariance adaptation then reinforced that direction. A smaller population with more generations is the obvious change. One seed only.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.303 places this eleventh of thirteen. The result is bimodal: 0.611 on deco_hop, which is the third best in the round, and 0.443 on zaleplon_mpo, against 0.064 on drd2_docking, which is the second worst any root recorded there. median_2 reached 0.208 and sitagliptin_mpo 0.187. Every mechanism check was exact. All 70 generations used full 24 by 24 covariance matrices with reconstructed rank-one and rank-mu terms, the recomputed learning constants matched, the cumulative path and step-size control were independently reproduced through eigendecomposition of each covariance, and every one of the accepted offspring joined its exact generating latent and score.

molecular.headline: Latent drift into large lipophilic molecules, with aromatic content collapsing on the objectives it loses
molecular.overall_character: The population varies more by objective than any other root, which is what covariance adaptation in a latent space would be expected to produce. Where it does well, aromatic content reaches 86 to 95 percent with molecules around forty to fifty-nine characters. Where it fails, aromatic content drops to 36 and 49 percent and molecules balloon to eighty characters of fluorinated ethers and alkyl chains. Ring closure stays high throughout at 87 to 99 percent, so the decoder is producing closed structures; what changes is whether those rings are aromatic and whether the molecule stays a reasonable size.

per_task.generated_character: Fused acridine-like amides averaging forty-one characters with 86 percent aromatic content, but the lowest halogen rate on the node at 8 percent.
liabilities: cyclic imine bridges hydrolyse under physiological conditions
enol ether termini appear throughout and are acid labile
missing_features: halogen substitution, present in under a tenth of proposals
stable ring fusions rather than the imine bridges in the top scorers
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best at 0.443 is a diarylamine fused through an imine into a tricyclic, and it is the node's second strongest objective. The zero scorers are large open chains carrying multiple amide and ester groups, so the latent region here stayed compact where on other objectives it did not.

per_task.generated_character: The node's best objective and third best in the round. Halogenated benzamides linked to fused polyaza aromatics, averaging fifty-nine characters with 94 percent aromatic content and near-total ring closure.
liabilities: chains of three and four consecutive N=C imine bonds are not stable functional groups
an alpha-keto ester in the top scorer is hydrolytically labile
missing_features: stable amide linkers in place of the repeated N=C imine chains in the high scorers
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top four cluster between 0.595 and 0.611 and all share a substituted benzoate amide joined to a nitrogen-rich fused ring. The bottom of the range drops the fused aromatic for sulfone-bridged enones. Where the latent Gaussian stayed in aromatic territory, this method performs well.

per_task.generated_character: The clearest failure on this node. Proposals average eighty characters, nearly double every other objective here, with only 49 percent aromatic content and long fluorinated alkyl and ether chains dominating.
liabilities: extended perfluoroalkyl chains carry no drug-likeness and high lipophilicity
geminal diols and hemiketal-like centres appear among the top scorers
missing_features: a protonatable aliphatic amine, absent from the entire top of the range
compact molecules; this set averages eighty characters against forty for the winners
simple fused aromatic bicyclics such as indoles
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The whole population spans 0.0002 to 0.064, so there is no gradient to climb. Not one proposal carries the basic amine on a compact aromatic that other roots used to reach above 0.9. The top scorers are large spirocyclic ethers with pendant fluorophenyl chains, which is the wrong region entirely.

per_task.generated_character: The node's most aromatic set at 95 percent with ring closure at 99.7 percent, averaging forty-nine characters of benzodioxole-substituted biaryls and fused lactams, and almost no halogen at 5 percent.
liabilities: cross-conjugated ketoamides among the low scorers are reactive
missing_features: molecules positioned between the two similarity targets rather than near one
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best at 0.208 is the third highest on this objective in the round, and it is also the smallest molecule in its own top four, a simple ethoxyphenyl benzodioxole. Scores fall away into open conjugated amides, so compactness and ring content are what the objective is rewarding here.

per_task.generated_character: Only 36 percent of proposals carry an aromatic atom and 13 percent close no ring, averaging thirty-six characters of partially saturated conjugated rings and open enones.
liabilities: acrylamide and cross-conjugated enone groups are Michael acceptors
terpenoid-like polycyclic hydrocarbons are not candidates for this objective
missing_features: aromatic rings, absent from nearly two thirds of proposals
fluorinated substituents, present in only 13 percent of proposals
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best reaches 0.187 against a median of 0.0001. The top entries are small partially saturated pyridines and acrylamides, while the zero scorers are large terpenoid and steroid-like polycycles with long alkyl chains, which is the same latent drift toward lipophilic bulk seen on the objective it lost.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On the objective it loses worst, proposals average eighty characters against thirty-six to fifty-nine on the same node's other objectives, with aromatic content falling to 49 percent and long perfluoroalkyl chains dominating the top of the range.
transferable_gaps.gap: the sampling distribution drifts into large lipophilic regions and then reinforces the drift
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Adapting a covariance on ranked samples amplifies whatever direction the early generations happened to favour, so a bad early drift becomes self-reinforcing rather than self-correcting. A bound on the sampled region, or a restart when the population's character shifts, is what this asks for.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each objective completed exactly fourteen generations of twenty scored offspring, while a full 24 by 24 covariance with rank-one and rank-mu updates needs far more to become informative.
transferable_gaps.gap: the search has too few generations to finish adapting its covariance
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Spending a fixed budget on twenty samples per generation buys covariance estimates that never converge. Fewer samples per generation and more generations would let the adaptation mechanism actually do its work within the same number of evaluations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The second and third highest-scoring molecules on one objective each carry three or four consecutive N=C linkages in a single chain, and similar chains appear throughout that population.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator writes chains of consecutive imine bonds
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The decoder can repeat an imine token indefinitely because nothing checks that the resulting chain is a real functional group. Capping consecutive heteroatom double bonds at emission removes these without constraining the latent search.

method_name: CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder
method_thesis: Anchor the optimizer in CMA-ES: sample a multivariate Gaussian, rank evaluated samples, move its mean by weighted recombination, and adapt covariance and step size using selected displacements and cumulative evolution paths. [Hansen, Sections 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1604.00772v2) describes this mechanism. For the molecular transfer, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder. Each objective starts with fresh Gaussian and path state. Encodings of high-scoring supplied molecules may initialize geometric search locations, but their scores must not be assigned to nonidentical reconstructions. Generate latent samples, decode them into new molecules, and attach accepted oracle feedback to the exact latent sample that produced each submitted structure. Assemble scored generations while respecting the evaluator-announced batching, then update the Gaussian from descending observed-score ranks. Reject invalid or duplicate structures locally and continue de novo decoding. The corpus trains a generator and never supplies a ranked molecular library. The hypothesis is that learning correlated latent displacements directly from successful generations can uncover improving combinations without first estimating an objective surrogate, increasing the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Useful decoder support and covariance adaptation within scarce feedback are empirical prerequisites; continuous-domain performance is not evidence that decoded molecular landscapes will behave similarly.
